metadata.title: Nvidia, AMD, Micron stocks lead chip sector higher amid Anthropic IPO optimism

content.text:
Chip giants Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) rose on Thursday amid growing optimism as investors prepared for Anthropic to start trading in what is one of the most hotly anticipated IPOs ever. Other chipmakers, including Broadcom (AVGO) and Intel (INTC), also gained.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) jumped 4%, along with peer SK Hynix (SKHY).
Micron president and chief technology officer Scott DeBoer reiterated on Deirdre Bosa Live on Wednesday that memory supply in 2027 will be tighter than in 2026.
"Our supply, we don't see it coming into balance with demand really in any time we can actually pick in the future right now," he said.
The broader chip sector rose on Thursday, helping lift the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) following recent volatile sessions, as the exit of Jensen Huang as CEO at Nvidia and concerns over AI financing have created jitters across the AI trade.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) and equipment maker ASML (ASML) also gained on Thursday, leading the Technology (XLK) sector higher.
Other areas of the AI trade also rose on Thursday, with optical equipment maker Coherent (COHR) up 7%. Bloom Energy (BE) shares also jumped, while shares of neocloud providers CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) both increased by more than 4%.
"Anthropic's IPO is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI Revolution growth thesis is not waning," Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives said on Wednesday evening.
The analyst noted that the AI trade is going through "a very turbulent, white-knuckle period that does not change our longer-term view that $3 trillion to $4 trillion of capex will be spent over the next few years."
The frontier lab's IPO "sets the stage for the next phase of tech and infrastructure investment with Anthropic a central player in the buildout," Ives added.
